SIM-3 QUALIFIED & LIVE

3D Kinematic Tree Studio

An interactive, zero-dependency 3D browser workbench powered by our analytical C++ dynamics engine compiled to WebAssembly (ABI 2). Inspect multi-link articulated chains with live matrix readouts.

  • 1-, 2-, and 3-Link Dynamics: Nonlinear pendulum, double pendulum, and 3-DOF articulated robot arm
  • Interactive 3D Orbit Viewport: Zero-dependency perspective projection with drag-to-orbit yaw/pitch and scroll zoom
  • Real-Time Analytical Inspectors: Live Mass Matrix M(q), Coriolis vector, gravity vector g(q) = ∇U, and End-Effector Jacobian J(q)
  • Mechanical Energy Tracking: Kinetic (K), Potential (U), and Total (E) conserved within 1e-4 drift
  • Governed Contracts: Model schema seedcore.mini-sim.tree-model.v1 with canonical SHA-256 digests and JSON export

PRACTICAL HARDWARE ARCHITECTURE

The $150 Fast Spine Maker Blueprint

Mini-robots do not need $3,000 industrial SoCs. Build an agile, safe-by-physics physical AI embodiment with off-the-shelf maker electronics.

$150 BILL OF MATERIALS

Consumer Maker Hardware

Microcontroller: ESP32-S3 or Raspberry Pi RP2040 ($6).
Actuators: 4–6x Feetech STS3215 magnetic encoder serial bus servos ($60–$80).
Power: 2S LiPo (7.4V) or 5V USB-C PD ($15).
Chassis: 3D-printed PETG / PLA / TPU ($10).
Camera: USB UVC webcam or ESP32-CAM ($12).

Total BOM: ~$150. Accessible for makers, students, and children.

FAST SPINE FIRMWARE

200–500 Hz Spline Interpolator

The edge MCU fast spine runs a deterministic hardware timer interrupt. It receives receding-horizon action chunks (30–50 waypoints) from the host brain over UART/WebSerial.

Evaluates smooth cubic Hermite spline trajectories locally and drives servos over 1 Mbps half-duplex UART bus with zero communication jitter.

Includes hardware watchdog: brings motors to rest if packets cease for > 100ms.

ZERO-INSTALL WEBSERIAL

Browser Direct-to-MCU Bridge

Using the W3C WebSerial API, any browser running on a Chromebook, Mac, or Windows PC can connect directly to the robot's USB-CDC port without installing drivers, ROS 2, or Linux.

Deploy trained neural policies, send action chunks, inspect live proprioception, and verify cryptographic receipts directly in the web browser.

BEGINNER & MAKER QUICKSTART

Zero-Soldering Desktop Connection

Building your first desktop robot shouldn't require electrical engineering. Here is exactly how the consumer hardware connects on your desk.

STEP 1: SNAP & PLUG

Zero Soldering Wiring

Each Feetech STS3215 bus servo features two identical 3-pin snap sockets. Plug the first cable from your ESP32 board to Servo 1, then daisy-chain from Servo 1 to Servo 2, and Servo 2 to Servo 3. Total wiring time: under 3 minutes.

STEP 2: ONE-CLICK CONNECT

Browser WebSerial Pairing

Plug the ESP32 into your computer via USB-C. Open 3D Tree Studio in Chrome, Edge, or Opera. Click "Connect USB" and pick your device in the standard browser popup. No drivers or baud rate configuration needed.

STEP 3: SLIDERS & TEACH MODE

Immediate Responsive Motion

Move the joint sliders on your screen—the physical servos track each angle in real time. Switch on "Teach Mode" to gently guide the arm by hand; the browser records your exact motion path for automated playback.
